summary: Willamette NF lookout site in Lane County, OR: tower built 1930, abandoned 1969, now gone; reached by Forest Service trail #3688 from an open trailhead.

facts.status_note: Lookout abandoned in 1969 and described as gone; no source describes remains at the site
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Willamette National Forest

access.note: Reached on foot by Forest Service Moon Point Trail #3688 from the Moon Point Trailhead, which the agency lists as open. No lookout structure to visit.

visit.trail_note: Moon Point Trail #3688 from the Moon Point Trailhead; agency directions run from Highway 58 two miles east of Oakridge through Forest Roads 21 and 2129

events.note: Register: a tower was built on the site in 1930; Firelookout.com says only 'the 1930s'
Lookout site abandoned in 1969 (register and Forest Lookouts agree)
Registered November 18, 2019 in the Former Fire Lookout Sites Register, nominated by Tammy McLeod

evidence.quote: Moon Point was once the site of a fire lookout.

evidence.supports: tower built on the site in 1930
evidence.quote: A tower was built on the site in 1930.
The lookout was abandoned in 1969 and is gone.

evidence.supports: reached on foot; trail leads hikers to the point
evidence.quote: Moon Point Trail leads the hiker to a unique area

evidence.supports: trail crosses wet and dry meadows and rocky cliffs
evidence.quote: The trail crosses wet and dry meadows, rocky cliffs, and passes beneath high-elevation conifers.

evidence.supports: directions begin on Highway 58 two miles east of Oakridge
evidence.quote: Proceed 2 miles east from Oakridge, Oregon on Highway 58 to Kitson Springs Road.

evidence.supports: 18 miles on Road 21 to junction with Road 2129
evidence.quote: Turn right and proceed for .5 miles to Road 21. Turn right and continue for 18 miles to junction with Road 2129.

evidence.supports: about 7 miles on Road 2129 then 1.5 miles to the trailhead
evidence.quote: Turn left and follow Forest Road 2129 for approximately 7 miles to Forest Road 2129-439 and driving 1.5 miles to the Moon Point Trailhead.

evidence.supports: view takes in the Middle Fork Ranger District and the Umpqua National Forest
evidence.quote: From here enjoy the view of the Middle Fork Ranger District and the Umpqua National Forest.

evidence.supports: register describes the lookout as gone
evidence.quote: The lookout was abandoned in 1969 and is gone.

sources.title: Moon Point Trail #3688
sources.publisher: Willamette National Forest, USDA Forest Service

sources.title: Moon Point Trailhead
sources.publisher: Willamette National Forest, USDA Forest Service

notes_for_editor: Built year 1930 comes from the register alone; Firelookout.com only says 'the 1930s'. Abandonment in 1969 is in two sources. No design, height, staffing or fire record found in the sources read. What, if anything, remains at the site is unknown. Access is by the Forest Service trail; the record's access 'unknown' can be updated to public.
